terms.gloss: the original (from which copies are made)
terms.comment: A rare Greek word (Lewis & Short). As an adjective, archetypus: Martial’s poems in his own hand are archetypae nūgae (Mart. 7.11.4), and Juvenal’s philosophers’ busts are “originals” (Juv. 2.7).

evidence: Suet. Aug. 71: autographā quādam epistulā (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The original of a letter or a manuscript, in the author’s hand; as a noun, autographum, an autograph (Symmachus; M-O s.v. original text or manuscript).

phrases.latin: Cōgis mē calamō manūque nostrā ēmendāre meōs, Pudēns, libellōs. Ō quam mē nimium probās amāsque, quī vīs archetypās habēre nūgās!
phrases.english: You make me correct my little books, Pudens, with my own pen and hand. Oh, how much too highly you rate me and love me, to want my trifles in the original!

sources: Lewis & Short: archetypus · Lewis & Short: autographus
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. original subst.; original text or manuscript.
